sam_cust: Hey team — after the model upgrade yesterday our embeddings started coming back with length 1024 (used to be 768). This broke our ingest pipeline. Example single-request response we just hit:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood/embed-large-pt",
  "input": "test"
}

HTTP 200
{
  "data": [{ "embedding": [0.12, 0.03, ... /* 1024 floats */ ] }],
  "metadata": {"vec_len": 1024}
}
```
We rolled a pinned variant yesterday (project pinned to locked-v2026-02 -> locked-v2026-03). Can you confirm?

maria_support: Sorry about the break — we see a few similar reports, will triage. Can you paste the model name + pinned variant you see in your dashboard and one request_id from a failing response?

sam_cust: Model: redwood/embed-large-pt, Project pin shows `locked-v2026-03-14` (we pinned in the UI). Request header had `x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d`. Batch size was 16 originally; I also tried single input and still got 1024.

leo_engineer: Thanks. Quick question: did you ever force a specific variant in the `x-redwood-model` header or query? Any chance your routing fell back to a new variant variant that changed output dims? Also can you run a single direct curl against the variant explicitly to confirm? Example: 
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "x-redwood-model: redwood/embed-large-pt:locked-v2026-02" 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
That should show the old 768 length.

sam_cust: We can't hit locked-v2026-02 directly because it's under reserved capacity for a different customer. The UI shows our project pinned to locked-v2026-03-14. Single request to the default endpoint returns 1024. Here is a trimmed response (single input):
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.01,0.02,... /* 1024 floats */]}],"model":"redwood/embed-large-pt:locked-v2026-03-14","request_id":"req_0a1b2c3d"}
```

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: model `redwood/embed-large-pt:locked-v2026-03-14` rolled out to hosted cluster eu-west-1 at 2026-03-14T17:10:12Z (author: infra-release).

irene_oncall: @leo_engineer :eyes: this looks like a model artifact shape change during onboarding. Could be that the locked variant actually points to a different model family (dense dim=1024) — routing fallback or alias may have been remapped. Please check variant-to-artifact mapping and any recent alias changes.

leo_engineer: Copy. Actionables: 1) ask provisioning/routing logs for any alias remap for that project, 2) try to temporarily revert the project's mapping to the previous artifact if available, 3) if revert not possible, open rollback on hosted cluster. Can you also share one full response header blob (we need the `x-redwood-variant` + `x-request-id`) from the failing call?

sam_cust: Full headers from the failing request: 
```
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
x-redwood-variant: locked-v2026-03-14
content-type: application/json
```
We can't change routing on our side because the project pin is managed in your console. Immediate mitigation for us would be to route to older dims or pause ingestion.

maria_support: Thanks, creating internal incident REDWOOD-INC-5423 and tagging eng-runtime + infra-release. We'll gather variant mappings and recent deploy diffs. I'll request a rollback window and notify you here.

leo_engineer: Quick triage note: reproduce confirmed with the provided request_id. Logs show artifact `embed-large-v2.1` (1024-dim) was associated with `locked-v2026-03-14` during onboarding. Likely cause: variant alias pointed at new artifact by mistake. Plan: roll project pin back to `locked-v2026-02` mapping for this customer; if that mapping is unavailable due to reserved capacity constraints, we'll provision a compatibility shim that trims/pads to expected 768 for your ingestion. ETA ~2 hours. :hourglass:

irene_oncall: Please avoid ingesting the 1024 vectors into downstream indices until we confirm rollback or shim. If you have schema validation in Kafka/DB, hold there.

sam_cust: Understood — we'll pause ingestion and wait for your update. Please escalate if rollback will take longer. Thanks for the quick responses. :thumbsup:
